Therefore, when it is said that Joseph should go and see the peace of his brothers, it signifies His coming. Every coming is said to take place when truth flows into the thought from the Word.

4713. **And the peace of the flock,** which signifies how it stands with those who learn or the Church, is evident from the signification of "peace," as how one’s state is <note>concerning which see just above, n. 4712</note>; and from the signification of the "flock," as those who learn. For a shepherd or one who feeds is one who teaches and leads to the good of charity, and the flock consists of those who learn and are led <note>concerning which see n. 343</note>, and thus it also signifies the Church.

4714. **And bring me back word,** which signifies knowledge, is evident from the signification of "bringing back a word," which is to report how the matter stands, thus knowledge.

4715. **And he sent him out of the valley of Hebron,** which signifies from the Divine Natural and Sensual, is evident from the signification of being "sent," as to proceed and to teach <note>concerning which see above, n. 4710</note>; from the signification of a "valley," as those things which are below <note>concerning which see n. 1723, 3417</note>; and from the signification of "Hebron," as the Lord’s Church as to good <note>concerning which see n. 2909</note>. Thus, these words signify that He would teach those things which are lower in the Church, and this because they would not grasp the higher things. For one who teaches faith and not charity can never perceive the higher or interior things of the Church. He does not have anything that leads or dictates whether this is of faith or whether this is true. But if he teaches charity, then he has good; this is a dictate to him and leads him, for all truth is from good and acts concerning good. Or, what is the same, all of faith is from charity and acts concerning charity. That every doctrine regards the life is something anyone can know from natural light alone. 

That these words signify "from the Divine Natural and Sensual" is the higher sense. For those things which are lower in the Church are said to be from the Divine Natural and Sensual of the Lord. This is not because these things are lower in the Lord, for in the Lord and in His Divine Human everything is Infinite, as He is Jehovah as to both Essences <note>n. 2156, 2329, 2921, 3023</note>. Rather, it is because this is how it is with man. Those who are sensual men perceive the things in the Lord and from the Lord sensually, and those who are natural perceive them naturally. It is described this way based on the quality of those who receive it. Those who are celestial men, however, and thus truly rational, perceive interior things. It is said of them that they are taught from the Divine Rational of the Lord. This is the higher sense, as stated, which is signified by those words. 

That "valleys" are the lower things of the Church can be seen from other places in the Word, as in Isaiah: "The prophecy <note>original: "Propheticum"</note> of the valley of vision; what is it to you here, that you have all gone up to the rooftops? A day of tumult, and of treading down, and of perplexity to the Lord Jehovih Zebaoth, in the valley of vision" <note>XXII: 1, 5</note>. The "valley of vision" stands for fantasies about spiritual things from sensual things, thus from lower things. In the same: "The choice of your valleys were filled with a chariot, and the horsemen in placing themselves have set themselves at the gate" <note>XXII: 7</note>. The "choice of valleys" stands for goods and truths in the natural or external man. In the same: "The voice of one crying in the desert: prepare the way of Jehovah, make level in the solitude a path for our God, every valley shall be exalted" <note>XL: 3, 4</note>. <summary>This page explains that the "valley of Hebron" represents the lower or natural and sensual levels of the Church where the Lord's truth is received according to the capacity of the learner. It emphasizes that charity is the necessary guide for perceiving interior spiritual truths, whereas those focused only on faith remain in the lower, sensual interpretations.</summary>
